<reason>A genuinely close, high-quality exchange. PRO (B) set the more intuitive frame — the metric is whether a fifteen-year-old ever encounters the institution, "prioritize" only reallocates the marginal pound, and destinations already exist so the error is recoverable. Its pressure question about how a seventeen-year-old discovers a new channel was the sharpest in the debate, and its closing "my motion wearing a coat" landed on CON's concession that discovery happens via platform trailers. But CON (A) did more damage with PRO's own words: it turned "hands them to the platforms at twelve with nothing waiting" into a case for building the owned 13–25 service, turned "already paid for" into "static shelf built for her parents," and turned "some audience follows the face" into proof that creator partnerships rent attention. CON also answered both pressure questions directly with A1/A2 and then narrowed the whole dispute to "the marginal pound is the hour" versus "you can always commission another hour," giving a clean reason the one-click encounter is the truly unrecoverable failure. PRO's claim that CON "never answered Q1" was mistimed (CON had not yet spoken), and PRO's closing only partially met the static-destination point. Both openings were clipped equally. CON edges it on exploitation of concessions and progression; PRO had the more memorable lines.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 reversal of PRO's "nothing waiting at twelve" and "already paid for" lines — arguing PRO had described exactly the gap an owned youth service fills and then proposed to fill it with clips — materially damaged PRO's "destination already exists, we lose nothing" risk-asymmetry route, which PRO's closing did not fully repair.</best_rebuttal>
